title: Title and Chapter List
english: Testimonies of the holy and blessed Epiphanius, Archbishop of Constantia in Cyprus, from the God-inspired and holy Scriptures, concerning the coming of the only-begotten God the Word from heaven to earth, the wonders done through Him, His passion and resurrection, and His second appearing, which is yet to come.
1. That the Son was begotten before the ages.
2. That He was with the Father.
3. That He is co-creator.
4. That He was sent.
5. That He will come.
6. That He was seen, and that, being God, He became man.
7. That the Lord is of the seed of David.
8. That He comes from a virgin.
9. That after He is born He will keep the mother who bore Him a virgin.
10. That the womb is a gate.
11. That the virgin will give birth without pangs.
12. That He was anointed.
13. That on earth He is without a father and without intercourse.
14. That He is a child.
15. That He will be born in Bethlehem.
16. That the Magi will worship Him.
17. That the star will rise (Numbers 24:17).
18. That the infants will be slain.
19. That Herod will be troubled, and all who are with him.
20. That he will seek, in pretence, to worship Him.
21. That he will be enraged at being deceived.
22. That he will search and make inquiry.
23. That he will kill the infants.
24. That he will not kill the Christ.
25. That Christ will go down into Egypt.
26. That He will be called out of Egypt.
27. That, when He is baptized, He will sanctify the waters.
28. That He will come up from the baptism in glory.
29. That He will walk on the sea.
30. That the hem of His garment will heal.
31. That He will wither the fig tree.
32. That He will be tempted by the devil.
33. That He will heal many.
34. That He will raise the dead.
35. That the Jews will not believe.
36. That from five loaves He will feed many.
37. That He will enter Zion on a donkey.
38. That the little children will run ahead of Him, crying, “Blessed is He who comes” (Psalm 118:26; Matthew 21:9).
39. That He will rebuke the people.
40. That nard will be poured over Him.
41. That they will gather together against Him.
42. That they will bear false witness against Him.
43. That Judas will betray Him.
44. That Judas will say, “Greetings, Rabbi” (Matthew 26:49).
45. That He will be sold for silver.
46. That they will bind Christ.
47. That they will put Him on trial.
48. That they will strike Him and treat Him with contempt.
49. That the apostles will flee.
50. That Peter will deny Him.
51. That they will crucify Him.
52. That they will crown Him with thorns.
53. That they will give Him vinegar and gall to drink (Psalm 69:21).
54. That they will clothe Him in a scarlet robe.
55. That He will keep silent when He is tried.
56. That He will be mocked.
57. That He who hangs on the tree is Himself the Life.
58. That His suffering is freedom from suffering.
59. That He will suffer at night, while it is cold and a charcoal fire has been laid (John 18:18).
60. That the sun will set.
61. That the sun will set at noon (Amos 8:9).
62. That they will divide His garments among themselves (Psalm 22:18).
63. That He will be crucified with robbers.
64. That they will pierce His side.
65. That not one of His bones will be broken (Exodus 12:46; John 19:36).
66. That water will flow from His side as a figure of baptism.
67. That He will be laid in a rock.
68. That the door of the tomb is a stone.
69. That they will set a seal on Him.
70. That He will be buried.
71. That the passion will take place as summer begins, in the month we call March.
72. That, once buried, He will strike Hades with fear.
73. That He is without sin.
74. That He will rise again.
75. That the soldiers will guard the tomb in vain.
76. That the resurrection is at dawn.
77. That the place will be a witness.
78. That it is by the outer wall.
79. That He will be sought by the women.
80. That He will first meet women.
81. That they will go away in fear.
82. That He will breathe the Holy Spirit upon the apostles.
83. That after the resurrection He will eat honey from the comb.
84. That they will say He was stolen.
85. That the dead will rise.
86. That He will go up into the heavens.
87. That He Himself was the one who preached.
88. That His name is in all the earth.
89. That He took His seat at the right hand of the Father not from the time He ascended, but even before that.
90. That we shall be called Christians.
91. That the marking of the cross on the forehead was also foretold.
92. That baptism in Christ was foretold.
93. That the second coming was foretold.

translator_notes: This section is the work’s title and its list of chapter headings 1-94; the list runs on to heading 102 in the next section. Greek letter numerals are given as Arabic numbers.

The printed list has lost two Greek numerals, those for 6 and 90: the headings 6, 16, 26, 36, 46, 56, 66, 76 and 86 show incomplete numbers and heading 90 has none. The numbers are restored from the headings in the body of the work.
The Latin line “Testimonia ex divinis et sacris scripturis” at the head is the edition’s label (already the page title) and is not rendered.

Heading 1: the list spells γεγένηται (“came to be”); the heading in the body reads γεγέννηται (“has been begotten”), which fits Epiphanius’s doctrine and the proof text (Psalm 110:3 in the Greek). Rendered “begotten”.
Heading 12: the list’s ἐχρήσθη is a misspelling of ἐχρίσθη, as the heading in the body reads and its proof texts (Psalm 45:7; Isaiah 61:1) confirm. Rendered “anointed”.
Heading 8 has no verb in the Greek; “comes from” supplies the bare link without adding “born”.
βρέφη is “infants” in 18 and 23 (the slaughter at Bethlehem) and “little children” in 38, where they run and cry out.
Heading 58 keeps the wordplay of the Greek: His suffering does not touch the Godhead, which cannot suffer. “Freedom from suffering” is kept plain rather than the technical “impassibility”.
Heading 59 takes the cold and the charcoal fire from John 18:18; the proof text in the body is Zechariah 14:6. In the body the heading names the subject (“Christ”); the list leaves it implied.
Headings 70 and 71 stand in the reverse order in the body (there 70 is the passion in March and 71 the burial). The list order is kept here.

Heading 77: μαρτύριον may also point to the Martyrium, Constantine’s basilica over Golgotha. Heading 78 has no verb; “it” is the place of 77, and the testimony under 78 cites Song of Solomon 2:14 (“close by the outer wall”). The Greek may mean “just outside” the wall.
Heading 87: the testimonies under 87 cite Isaiah 61:1 and 52:6 (“I Myself am the one who speaks”), so “He Himself was the one who preached” means that the speaker in the prophets is Christ.

Heading 89: the list moves the words “but even before that” to after heading 90; the heading in the body keeps them in place, with the negation (“not from the time He ascended”). Rendered from the body.

Possible allusions left without inline citation because the headings summarise rather than quote: 7 (Romans 1:3), 63 (Isaiah 53:12), 64 (Zechariah 12:10; John 19:34), 83 (Luke 24:42, where “honeycomb” stands only in part of the manuscript tradition; the testimony under 83 cites Song of Solomon 5:1), 88 (Psalm 8:1; the body cites other texts), 89 (Psalm 110:1).

The section ends partway through heading 94, which continues at the start of the next section (the full heading in the body reads “That He will judge the world, and judgment will be given to Him”). The English ends with an ellipsis so the next section can open with “world”.
